subject: Fwd: Request for benchmark attestation letter (Dedicated) — Redpine Fintech
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Fwd: Request for benchmark attestation letter (Dedicated) — Redpine Fintech

Looping you in per PM-612. Redpine is asking for a “benchmark attestation” letter as part of vendor approval.

They want something they can attach to their internal risk/procurement packet stating:
- tests were run by Redwood (or under Redwood supervision)
- the environment was controlled (hardware + driver/CUDA pinned)
- the results reflect the stated workload profile
- signed by an exec/leadership

I’m not sure what we’re comfortable signing to (esp. around “representative of production” language). Can we align on:
1) what we can disclose (hardware SKU? region? model variant? harness SHA?)
2) who signs
3) whether we provide a redacted results table vs methodology-only

Attaching the customer’s request PDF.

Attachment: Redpine_Request_Benchmark_Attestation.pdf (PDF)

—
Lauren Bishop
Product, Redwood Dedicated
Redwood Inference


---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@redpinefintech.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Arjun Nair <arjun.nair@redpinefintech.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 8:41 AM PST
Subject: Request for benchmark attestation letter (Dedicated)

Hi Lauren,

As part of our vendor onboarding process, our procurement team needs an attestation letter covering the benchmark results you shared last week.

Specifically, we need a letter on Redwood letterhead that confirms:
- the benchmarks were executed by Redwood Inference
- the benchmark environment (hardware, driver/CUDA versions) was controlled
- the workload parameters used (prompt/output length ranges, concurrency, streaming) match what we provided
- the results provided correspond to those runs

A signature from a VP-level sponsor is typically sufficient.

If you have a standard template, that’s fine. We do not need proprietary details, but we do need enough specificity to tie the letter to the run.

Thanks,
Maya

Maya Rao
Vendor Management, Redpine Fintech



From: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for benchmark attestation letter (Dedicated) — Redpine Fintech

We can do a limited attestation, but we need to be precise about what we’re asserting.

Proposed guardrails (consistent w/ PM-612 direction):
- We can attest that Redwood ran the benchmark harness, on the stated environment, with the stated workload parameters, and that the attached summary was produced from those runs.
- We should NOT attest that results are “representative of production” generally, or guarantee they’ll match their deployment if they change prompts, concurrency, routing, etc.

Disclosure: I’m comfortable with including:
- model identifier as used in Redwood catalog (e.g., “RW-Chat-70B vX.Y”)
- deployment mode: Dedicated
- region(s) where executed
- instance class + GPU type (but not fleet-level specifics)
- runtime build ID / commit SHA
- driver/CUDA major/minor
- workload definition (ranges / distributions), not the literal prompts

Signature: Mateo as Runtime exec sponsor would carry weight; otherwise Paula + Product sign-off + “Reviewed by Runtime” could work.

Lauren, if you want to draft, I can mark up.

Henry

—
Henry Cho
Product, Performance Transparency
Redwood Inference


From: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 12:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for benchmark attestation letter (Dedicated) — Redpine Fintech

Agree with Henry.

Two additions:
1) We need a consistent template + approval path so this doesn’t become bespoke each time. Let’s treat this as the first “customer attestation” variant under PM-612.
2) If we attach a results table, it must be “summary only” (e.g., TTFT p50/p95, TPOT p50/p95, throughput), and explicitly scoped to the run conditions.

Please avoid including:
- any mention of other customers / aggregated traffic
- anything that implies SLAs beyond contract language
- raw logs, request traces, or prompt artifacts

Mateo: if you’re willing to sign, we should keep it to a single page.

Paula

—
Paula Mendes
Product, Enterprise Rollouts & Approvals
Redwood Inference


From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 1:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for benchmark attestation letter (Dedicated) — Redpine Fintech

I’m okay signing a narrowly-scoped letter.

Non-negotiables:
- We attest to execution + configuration + that the attached summary came from those runs.
- We do not attest to “expected customer production performance” or anything forward-looking.
- Any environment details must be stable identifiers (GPU type, driver/CUDA, runtime build ID). No internal fleet hostnames or capacity details.

Lauren: draft it and send to us for final edits.

Also, confirm with the team that the run environment was cleanly pinned (INT-1440 is a reminder we’ve had drift issues). If there’s any doubt, we re-run rather than sign.

Mateo

Mateo Alvarez
VP Engineering, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference


From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 13, 2026 at 9:47 AM PST
Subject: Draft attestation letter for Redpine (v0.2)

Thanks all — draft attached.

What I included:
- Run date window + region
- “Dedicated benchmark environment” + GPU type + driver/CUDA
- Runtime build ID (git SHA) and harness version
- Workload parameters (streaming chat, prompt length range, output cap, concurrency ramp)
- Attachment A: a 6-line summary table (TTFT p50/p95, TPOT p50/p95, throughput)
- Explicit disclaimers per above

Open questions for approval:
1) Are we okay naming the model as “RW-Chat-70B v3.1” in the letter? (Not including underlying open-weight name.)
2) Do we list the exact instance type (e.g., “H100 SXM 80GB class”) vs “NVIDIA H100 80GB”?

Attachment: Redwood_Benchmark_Attestation_Letter_v0.2.docx (DOCX)

—
Lauren


From: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 13, 2026 at 11:21 AM PST
Subject: Re: Draft attestation letter for Redpine (v0.2)

Edits look good.

Answers:
1) Yes, “RW-Chat-70B v3.1” is the right level. Do not map to upstream model name in writing.
2) Prefer “NVIDIA H100 80GB” + cloud region. Avoid provider-specific instance SKU unless procurement explicitly requires it.

One tweak: in the disclaimer, add a line that performance may vary with:
- different prompt distributions (esp. long-context)
- different streaming chunking behavior/client networking
- different safety/tool-calling configs

If you update, I think Mateo can sign.

Henry


From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@redpinefintech.com>
Cc: Arjun Nair <arjun.nair@redpinefintech.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 14, 2026 at 4:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Request for benchmark attestation letter (Dedicated)

Hi Maya,

Sharing the attestation letter on Redwood letterhead covering the benchmark run and summary metrics, scoped to the exact workload parameters you provided.

A couple of notes called out in the letter as well:
- the attestation confirms execution/configuration and that the attached summary table corresponds to those runs
- it does not assert that all production performance will match outside the defined workload/environment

If your procurement team needs a specific format (e.g., your template language), send it over and we’ll review.

Best,
Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Product, Redwood Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Benchmark_Attestation_Letter_Redpine_Feb2026.pdf (PDF)
